title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The endpoint fetches a `Rule` or `AlertRule` object using a user-supplied `rule_id` from the URL path without verifying that the object belongs to the `project` provided in the URL. findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM methods (e.g., `Rule.objects.get`, `AlertRule.objects.get`, `RuleSnooze.objects.get_or_create`) which utilize parameterized queries and do not concatenate user input into SQL strings.

The endpoint fetches a `Rule` or `AlertRule` object using a user-supplied `rule_id` from the URL path without verifying that the object belongs to the `project` provided in the URL. While `ProjectEndpoint` ensures the user has access to the project, it does not restrict the `rule_id` to that project. An attacker with access to one project can snooze rules belonging to other projects by guessing or enumerating rule IDs (IDOR).
findings.suggested_fix: Filter the query by the project ID to ensure the rule belongs to the specified project. For example: `Rule.objects.get(id=rule_id, project=project)` and `AlertRule.objects.get(id=rule_id, projects__in=[project])`.
